definitions.name: Multiplicity-adjusted transform-zero instrument
definitions.construction: Given a zero \(z_0\) of \(M\) with multiplicity \(\ell\), set \(J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}e^{z_0w}\).

definitions.name: Observable contour functional
definitions.construction: For a positively oriented circle \(C_j\) on which \(F_n\) is zero-free and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), set \(\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)=\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_n(z)/F_n(z)\,dz\).

definitions.name: Once-for-all non-effective contour-bank witness
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathscr M\) be the locally uniform closure of the centered sub-Gaussian moment generating functions satisfying \(\lvert\kappa_k\rvert\ge\delta\).  A once-for-all contour bank is a tuple consisting of a finite \(J\ge1\), radii \((\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_J)\in(R_0,R_1)^J\), and \(a_{\star}>0\) such that, with \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\), every \(M\in\mathscr M\) has some \(j\) for which \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}\).  After \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) proves that such tuples exist, fix one arbitrary tuple and denote it by \((J,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_J,a_{\star})\).  The choice is deterministic and depends only on the class constants \((k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1)\); no effective enumeration, computable radii, computable modulus, or algorithm for finding the tuple is asserted.

statements.statement: If \(z_0\) is a zero of \(M\) of multiplicity \(\ell\), then for every real shift \(d\), \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]=0\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), this gives \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]=0\) and \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\); whenever this value is nonzero, \(\theta_0=E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]/E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\).
statements.justification: This exact identity displays the global location-family null score and its relevance under residual contamination.
statements.gap: Transform-zero incompleteness is classical, but its multiplicity-adjusted score has not been used to eliminate an arbitrary PLM covariate shift created by a supplied treatment code.
statements.consumer: Known-noise implementations can estimate the causal coefficient by a single bounded or exponentially weighted moment ratio.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(z_0\) be a zero of \(M\) of multiplicity \(\ell\). By the definition of multiplicity,
\[
M^{(j)}(z_0)=0\quad(0\le j<\ell),
\qquad
M^{(\ell)}(z_0)\ne0.
\]
The moment generating function \(M\) is entire by its declared definition. On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the sub-Gaussian bound on \(\eta\), the range restrictions \(\lVert g_0\rVert_\infty\le C_g\) and \(\bar g_n\in[-C_g,C_g]\), and the conditional sub-Gaussian bound on \(\xi\) ensure that every polynomial--exponential moment below is finite. Thus differentiation under the relevant expectations is justified by dominated convergence on each compact subset of \(\mathbb C\).

Fix \(d\in\mathbb R\), and define \(L_d(z)=E_P[e^{z(\eta+d)}]\). Since \(d\) is deterministic,
\[
L_d(z)=e^{zd}M(z).
\]
The derivative representation of an entire moment generating function and the Leibniz rule therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]
&=E_P[(\eta+d)^{\ell-1}e^{z_0(\eta+d)}]\\
&=L_d^{(\ell-1)}(z_0)\\
&=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}{\ell-1\choose j}
d^{\ell-1-j}M^{(j)}(z_0)\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last equality follows from the multiplicity relations. It includes the boundary case \(\ell=1\), for which the sum consists only of \(M(z_0)=0\).

Now fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\). The range restrictions imply
\[
|D_n|=|g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)|\le 2C_g
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The random variable \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), while \(\eta\perp X\) by \(\text{ass:independent-treatment-noise}\). Conditional on \(X\), apply the deterministic-shift identity with \(d=D_n\) to obtain
\[
E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]
=E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+D_n)\mid X]
=0
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]

Independence of \(\eta\) and \(D_n\) also yields, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[e^{z(\eta+D_n)}]=M(z)H_n(z).
\]
Because \(Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)=Z_n^\ell e^{z_0Z_n}\), differentiation followed by the Leibniz rule gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
&=F_n^{(\ell)}(z_0)\\
&=\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}{\ell\choose j}
M^{(j)}(z_0)H_n^{(\ell-j)}(z_0)\\
&=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every term with \(j<\ell\) vanishes, and the term \(j=\ell\) is the sole remaining term. Since \(M^{(\ell)}(z_0)\ne0\), the explicit relevance boundary condition is equivalently \(H_n(z_0)\ne0\); no further overlap or rank condition is used.

Finally, the residual definitions give
\[
Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi,
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0D_n.
\]
The class range restrictions make \(b_n\) bounded. Hence conditional annihilation implies
\[
E_P[b_n(X)J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=E_P\!\left[b_n(X)E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]\right]
=0.
\]
Moreover, \(J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\). By \(\text{ass:outcome-mean-independence}\),
\[
E_P[\xi J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\right]
=0.
\]
Multiplying the displayed structural decomposition by \(J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\) and taking expectations therefore yields
\[
E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=\theta_0E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)].
\]
Whenever \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\ne0\), division is valid and proves
\[
\theta_0
=\frac{E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}
{E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}.
\]
Thus the ratio is an identifying functional for the causal coefficient under the stated structural assumptions and the explicit nonzero-relevance boundary condition; the equality is derived rather than imposed by definition.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)\) and \(G_n(z)=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).
statements.justification: The identity recovers the latent transform-zero geometry from observable learned residuals and isolates an analytic nuisance ratio.
statements.gap: Classical convolution results do not provide the outcome transform \(G_n=\theta_0F_n'+MB_n\) for a partially linear causal coefficient.
statements.consumer: The contour theorem integrates \(G_n/F_n\) and removes \(B_n/H_n\) exactly.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(z\in\mathbb C\).  Since \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), the independence \(\eta\perp X\) gives
\[
 F_n(z)
 =E_P[e^{z(\eta+D_n)}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[e^{zD_n}]
 =M(z)H_n(z).
\]
All transforms in this display are entire: \(D_n\) is bounded by the clipping and range restrictions, while the sub-Gaussian bound on \(\eta\) supplies an integrable exponential envelope on every compact subset of \(\mathbb C\).  The same envelope permits differentiation under the expectation, so
\[
 F_n'(z)=E_P[Z_ne^{zZ_n}].
\]
Using the identity \(Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_n(z)
 &=\theta_0E_P[Z_ne^{zZ_n}]
   +E_P[b_n(X)e^{zZ_n}]
   +E_P[\xi e^{zZ_n}]\\
 &=\theta_0F_n'(z)
   +E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}e^{z\eta}].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, \(e^{zZ_n}\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), and therefore the outcome mean-independence restriction gives
\[
 E_P[\xi e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P\!\left[e^{zZ_n}E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\right]=0.
\]
Finally, \(b_n(X)e^{zD_n}\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), so a second use of \(\eta\perp X\) gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}e^{z\eta}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}]
 =M(z)B_n(z).
\]
Combining the displays proves both identities for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).

statements.statement: Let \(C_j\) be positively oriented. If \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\), \(H_n\) is zero-free on and inside \(C_j\), and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), then \(\theta_0=\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)=\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_n(z)/F_n(z)\,dz\).
statements.justification: The observable contour formula identifies the coefficient without learning the outcome regression or separating the two transform factors.
statements.gap: Location-family completeness and real-zero tests do not construct this observable complex contour functional for a PLM coefficient.
statements.consumer: The adaptive estimator evaluates the identifying functional on a pilot-selected contour.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{lem:observable-factorization}\), on the contour \(C_j\),
\[
 \frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}
   +\frac{M(z)B_n(z)}{M(z)H_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}+\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}.
\]
The first equality is valid because \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\).  The quotient \(B_n/H_n\) is analytic on and inside \(C_j\), because both functions are entire and \(H_n\) is zero-free there.  Cauchy's integral theorem therefore gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}\,dz=0.
\]
The argument principle and the assumed boundary zero-freeness give
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =N_{C_j}(F_n).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =\theta_0N_{C_j}(F_n).
\]
The assumed positive zero count licenses division by \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\).  The resulting expression is exactly \(\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)\) from \(\text{def:contour-functional}\), proving the claim.

statements.statement: There is \(A_k<\infty\), depending only on \(k\), such that every centered law with \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\) has a zero of \(M\) in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), where \(R_0\le A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\).
statements.justification: A uniform estimator requires usable spectral information in a disk fixed by primitive class constants.
statements.gap: Quantitative Marcinkiewicz results control Gaussian approximation from zero-free disks; this converse direction localizes a zero from fixed cumulant separation.
statements.consumer: The contour bank only searches the fixed disk determined here.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(c_{\psi}<\infty\) be the universal constant in the moment-generating-function consequence of the \(\psi_2\) bound:
\[
 E_P[e^{t\eta}]\le \exp(c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}t^{2}),
 \qquad t\in\mathbb R.
\]
This follows directly by expanding the exponential and using the sub-Gaussian moment bounds \(\|\eta\|_{L^p}\le C\psi_{\eta}\sqrt p\).  Hence, for complex \(z\),
\[
 |M(z)|\le E_P[e^{\operatorname{Re}(z)\eta}]
 \le \exp(c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}|z|^{2}).
\]

Fix \(R>0\) and suppose, toward a contradiction, that \(M\) has no zero in \(\{|z|\le R\}\).  Since the disk is simply connected and \(M(0)=1\), there is an analytic logarithm \(K=\log M\) on a neighborhood of the disk, normalized by \(K(0)=0\).  Put \(A=c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}R^{2}\).  The preceding display implies
\[
 \operatorname{Re}K(z)=\log|M(z)|\le A,
 \qquad |z|\le R.
\]
For completeness, the needed analytic bound follows without an additional probabilistic assumption.  The function
\[
 h(z)=\frac{K(z)}{2A-K(z)}
\]
satisfies \(|h(z)|\le1\), because
\[
 |2A-K(z)|^{2}-|K(z)|^{2}
 =4A\{A-\operatorname{Re}K(z)\}\ge0,
\]
and \(h(0)=0\).  Applying the Schwarz inequality after rescaling the radius-
\(R\) disk gives \(|h(z)|\le |z|/R\).  Thus, for \(|z|\le R/2\),
\[
 |K(z)|\le \frac{2A(|z|/R)}{1-|z|/R}\le2A.
\]
The Cauchy coefficient formula on \(|z|=R/2\) now yields
\[
 |\kappa_k(\eta)|=|K^{(k)}(0)|
 \le k!\frac{2A}{(R/2)^k}
 =2^{k+1}c_{\psi}k!\,\psi_{\eta}^{2}R^{2-k}.
\]
Choose
\[
 A_k=(2^{k+2}c_{\psi}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^{2}/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}.
\]
If \(M\) were zero-free on the radius-\(R_0\) disk, the preceding inequality would give \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\le\delta/2\), contradicting cumulant separation.  Therefore \(M\) has a zero with \(|z|\le R_0\).  This choice has the asserted dependence and, in particular, \(R_0\le A_k(\psi_{\eta}^{2}/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\), with equality for the displayed choice.

statements.statement: The construction in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) yields finite \(J\), radii \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and \(a_{\star}>0\) such that every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) with \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}\). The conclusion is uniform in \(n\).
statements.justification: Pointwise zero existence does not imply uniform risk; compact-open closure and boundary stability must produce a finite conditioned bank.
statements.gap: Existing pointwise transform-zero theory and zero-free-disk inequalities do not establish a finite contour cover uniform over this cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian class.
statements.consumer: A finite bank makes selection measurable and reduces stochastic control to finitely many contour ratios.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). For \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\le C_0h^2\), where \(c_0,C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants.
statements.justification: The lower bound uses an explicit Gaussian-outcome-innovation path that preserves the law of \((X,T)\), both regression functions, and the deterministic supplied codes.
statements.gap: A generic appeal to a parametric submodel does not verify membership in a triangular common-code class.
statements.consumer: Le Cam's two-point lemma turns this construction into the \(c/n\) half of the spectral minimax rate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and suppose that \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\).  Choose \(P_{\star}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  Retain from \(P_{\star}\) the joint law of \((X,T)\), the covariate marginal, the functions \(g_0\) and \(q_0\), and hence \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\).  The supplied codes and their clipped versions \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\) are deterministic experiment inputs and are retained as well.

Let
\[
 c_{\mathrm N}=\lVert N(0,1)\rVert_{\psi_2},
 \qquad
 \tau=\frac{\psi_{\xi}}{2c_{\mathrm N}}>0,
 \qquad
 c_0=\min\{C_{\theta},1\}>0.
\]
On a product extension, let \(\xi_{\star}\sim N(0,\tau^2)\) be independent of \((X,T)\).  For every \(\vartheta\in[-c_0,c_0]\), define
\[
 Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star},
\]
and let \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) be the resulting law of \((X,T,Y_{\vartheta})\).

We verify membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  The law of \((X,T)\) is unchanged, so \(g_0\), \(\eta\), the independence \(\eta\perp X\), the treatment sub-Gaussian bound, the order-\(k\) cumulant separation, the range bound on \(g_0\), and
\[
 \lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}
\]
are inherited from \(P_{\star}\).  Centering and independence of \(\eta\) give
\[
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta}}[Y_{\vartheta}\mid X]
 =q_0(X)+\vartheta E_{P_{\star}}[\eta\mid X]
 =q_0(X).
\]
Thus the outcome regression remains exactly \(q_0\), including \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\).  Conditional on \((X,T)\),
\[
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta}}[Y_{\vartheta}\mid X,T]
 =q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta,
 \qquad
 E[\xi_{\star}\mid X,T]=0.
\]
Hence the partially linear coefficient is \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\), and its outcome innovation is \(\xi_{\star}\).  This coefficient is unique: cumulant separation implies that \(\eta\) is not almost surely zero, so two distinct coefficients cannot give the same conditional mean.  The boundary condition holds because \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\le C_{\theta}\).  Finally, Gaussian scaling and independence yield
\[
 \lVert\xi_{\star}\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}
 =c_{\mathrm N}\tau
 =\frac{\psi_{\xi}}2
 \le\psi_{\xi}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Its variance \(\tau^2\) is strictly positive and depends only on the fixed class constant \(\psi_{\xi}\) and the universal norm convention.  Therefore \(P_{n,\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\).  No outcome-code restriction is used.

It remains to calculate the divergence.  The laws \(P_{n,\vartheta_0}\) and \(P_{n,\vartheta_1}\) have the same \((X,T)\) marginal.  Given \((X,T)\), their outcome distributions are Gaussian with common variance \(\tau^2>0\) and means differing by \((\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)\eta\).  The conditional chain rule for relative entropy and the equal-variance Gaussian density calculation give
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}\middle\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}\right)
 =\frac{(\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)^2}{2\tau^2}
 E_{P_{\star}}[\eta^2].
\]
The defining exponential-moment inequality for the \(\psi_2\)-norm implies, for a universal \(c_2<\infty\),
\[
 E_{P_{\star}}[\eta^2]\le c_2\psi_{\eta}^2.
\]
Additivity of relative entropy for product measures now shows that, whenever \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}
          \middle\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
 &=nD_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}
          \middle\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}\right)\\
 &=\frac{h^2}{2\tau^2}E_{P_{\star}}[\eta^2]\\
 &\le \frac{c_2\psi_{\eta}^2}{2\tau^2}h^2
 =:C_0h^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The constants \(c_0\) and \(C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants.  The only boundary conditions used are \(C_{\theta}>0\), \(\psi_{\xi}>0\), and cumulant separation; no propensity overlap, inverse, or rank condition is involved.

statements.statement:
There exist a once-for-all deterministic witness bank satisfying \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, after that one bank is fixed, the constants depend only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) and the associated statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is a measurable sample map for which the following holds.  For every \(n\ge2\) such that \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\),
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
This is an existence-level fixed-bank minimax result: no algorithm for obtaining the selected bank, its radii, or \(a_{\star}\) from the observations and displayed class constants is asserted.  After the selected bank is fixed, the statistic uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\).  Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to the separately defined subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\), select one once-for-all deterministic witness bank \((J,\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_J,a_{\star})\), and fix it throughout.  All constants below are allowed to depend on this selected finite tuple; because the lemma constructs the tuple from only \(k=r+1,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\), after fixation this is dependence only on the primitive class constants asserted in the theorem.  Write \(m_a=|I_a|\).  For \(n\ge2\), both halves are nonempty and \(m_a\ge n/3\).

Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  The selected bank supplies an index \(j_{\star}=j_{\star}(P)\) such that
\[
 N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(M)\ge1,
 \qquad \inf_{z\in C_{j_{\star}}}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
Since \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), \(\text{lem:l1-nuisance-zero-free}\) gives \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) on \(|z|\le R_1\), makes \(H_n\) zero-free there, and shows that \(F_n=MH_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros with multiplicity.  Hence
\[
 N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(F_n)\ge1,
 \qquad \inf_{z\in C_{j_{\star}}}|F_n(z)|\ge3a_{\star}/4. \tag{1}
\]

Put
\[
 d_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|,
 \qquad
 e_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_a=\{d_a\le a_{\star}/8\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_0\), (1) implies \(\inf_{C_{j_{\star}}}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\ge5a_{\star}/8\).  Rouch\'e's theorem gives
\[
 \widehat N_{0j_{\star},n}=N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(F_n)\ge1,
\]
so \(j_{\star}\) is pilot-admissible.  The finite maximizing rule therefore selects \(\widehat j_n\) with
\[
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\ge5a_{\star}/8,
 \qquad
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|F_n|\ge a_{\star}/2. \tag{2}
\]
A second application of Rouch\'e's theorem gives
\[
 \widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}=N_{C_{\widehat j_n}}(F_n)\ge1. \tag{3}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1\), (2) also gives \(\inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{1,n}|\ge3a_{\star}/8>a_{\star}/4\), so the evaluation fallback is not used.

Conditional on the selected bank, the selector and statistic are measurable.  Under every fixed circle parameterization, the empirical transforms and their derivatives are jointly measurable in the sample and continuous in the angle.  A boundary infimum equals the infimum over a fixed countable dense set of angles.  On the measurable zero-free event, the winding integral is the integral of a jointly measurable continuous integrand.  Finiteness of the bank and the deterministic tie and failure rules complete the measurability argument.  This establishes measurability after fixation and supplies no procedure for constructing the selected bank.

There is a class-uniform \(C_G<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|G_n(z)|\le C_G. \tag{4}
\]
Indeed, \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 |G_n(z)|\le e^{2C_gR_1}\|Y\|_{L^2(P)}
 \{E_P[e^{2R_1|\eta|}]\}^{1/2}.
\]
The bounds on \(q_0,\theta_0,\eta,\xi\) uniformly bound both factors.

On \(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1\), let \(C=C_{\widehat j_n}\) and \(N=N_{C_{\widehat j_n}}(F_n)\).  Equations (2)--(3), zero-freeness of \(H_n\), and \(\text{thm:exact-contour-identification}\) give
\[
 \theta_0=\frac{1}{N2\pi i}\oint_C\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz.
\]
The circle length is at most \(2\pi R_1\), \(N\ge1\), and the denominator bounds in (2) imply, by subtracting the two ratios,
\[
 \left|\frac{1}{N2\pi i}\oint_C
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}}{\widehat F_{1,n}}\,dz-\theta_0\right|
 \le L_{\star}(d_1+e_1), \tag{5}
\]
where \(L_{\star}<\infty\) depends only on the primitive constants after the selected bank is fixed.  Taking real parts and projecting onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase distance from the real number \(\theta_0\).

By \(\text{lem:empirical-transform-uniform-l2}\) and \(m_a\ge n/3\),
\[
 E_P[d_a^2+e_a^2]\le K_1/n. \tag{6}
\]
Markov's inequality yields
\[
 P(\mathcal A_0^c\cup\mathcal A_1^c)\le K_2/n. \tag{7}
\]
On the exceptional event, clipping bounds squared error by \(4C_{\theta}^2\).  Combining (5)--(7) proves uniformly in \(P\) that
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0)^2]
 \le2L_{\star}^2E_P[d_1^2+e_1^2]
 +4C_{\theta}^2P(\mathcal A_0^c\cup\mathcal A_1^c)
 \le C/n. \tag{8}
\]
The statistic associated with the selected bank is one measurable decision rule, so (8) also gives \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le C/n\).

For the converse, apply \(\text{lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}\).  Let \(c_0,C_0\) be its constants and choose
\[
 0<h\le\min\{c_0,1,(8C_0)^{-1/2}\},
 \qquad \vartheta_{\pm}=\pm h/(2\sqrt n).
\]
Both laws belong to the submodel, their target separation is \(h/\sqrt n\), and
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n})\le1/8.
\]
Pinsker's inequality gives total variation at most \(1/4\).  For an arbitrary estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), test with \(A=\{\widetilde\theta\ge0\}\).  On \(A\) under the negative law, or on \(A^c\) under the positive law, squared error is at least \(h^2/(4n)\).  Therefore
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-,+\}}E_{P_{n,\vartheta_v}}[(\widetilde\theta-\vartheta_v)^2]
 \ge \frac{h^2}{8n}\{1-\|P_-^{\otimes n}-P_+^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}
 \ge\frac{3h^2}{32n}.
\]
Taking the class supremum and estimator infimum proves the lower bound.

The selected-bank statistic uses only \(Y\), \(T-\bar g_n(X)\), and the fixed bank, not an outcome code or the law of \(\eta\).  Finally, (8) and Markov's inequality give
\[
 P\{|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0|>\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}\}\le\gamma,
\]
which is the asserted generalized-quantile bound.  The class disclaimer follows from the separate definitions of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).
statements.justification: Exact observable transform geometry and one non-effectively selected compactness witness yield a matched parametric decision-theoretic rate on the broad direct-\(L^1\) class.
statements.gap: Finite-order orthogonal and ACE results do not give exact all-shift annihilation or this existence-level fixed-bank uniform minimax theorem without an outcome learner; the theorem does not solve effective bank construction.
statements.consumer: The theorem establishes the fixed-separation minimax rate after one witness bank is selected, but supplies no algorithm for obtaining that bank, its radii, or \(a_{\star}\).

statements.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).  By
\(\text{def:ace-comparison-subclass}\), \(P\) satisfies every member property of
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and also
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]
Since \(P_X\) is a probability measure and \(s\ge r+1>r\), Lyapunov's inequality, with its usual \(L^{\infty}\) interpretation, gives
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}
 \le\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{1,n},
\]
and the identical argument gives
\[
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]
All remaining member properties in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) are already properties of the broad non-Gaussian class.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
This is only a one-way inclusion for the explicitly restricted comparison subclass; neither definition supplies either of the broader relations disclaimed in the statement.

Suppose next that \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds and
\(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\).  Applying
\(\text{lem:jms-ace-quantile-upper}\) on
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), and then restricting the supremum to the just-proved subclass, yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|)\\
 &\quad\le C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
 \Big[\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
 +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{31mm}
 +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
 \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
 (\gamma n)^{-1/2}\Big],
\end{aligned}
\]
which is exactly \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\).

It remains to justify the boundary value \(\varepsilon_{2,n}=0\).  Fix
\(u\in(0,\varepsilon_{1,n}]\), and temporarily enlarge only the outcome-code radius at index \(n\) from zero to \(u\).  Every law satisfying the zero-radius restriction also satisfies this enlarged restriction.  Moreover,
\[
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},u,
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}
 =
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},0,
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}.
\]
Thus \(b_{2,n}\), and hence the exact eligibility predicate, is unchanged.  The positive-radius result applied at radius \(u\) therefore gives the same left-hand side bounded by
\[
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
 \Big[\varepsilon_{1,n}^ru+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
 +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
 \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
 (\gamma n)^{-1/2}\Big].
\]
The left-hand side does not depend on \(u\).  Letting \(u\downarrow0\) proves the displayed boundary formula.  Positivity of \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) is exactly what permits this monotone extension without changing the maximum in the eligibility condition.

Finally suppose \(n\ge2\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\).  The comparison subclass is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  If it is nonempty, then the broad class is nonempty, so
\(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}};
\]
if it is empty, the uniform assertion is vacuous.  Along any asymptotic sequence on which
\[
 A_n:=\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
      +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
 \gg n^{-1/2},
\]
the fixed positive prefactors in \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\) give
\[
 B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\asymp A_n,
 \qquad
 n^{-1/2}=o(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}).
\]
Hence the spectral \(O(n^{-1/2})\) generalized-quantile guarantee is strictly smaller in order.  Only two upper guarantees have been compared; no risk lower bound for the ACE statistic follows.
statements.justification: The proposition isolates the exact subclass on which the published ACE comparison and its constants are licensed.
statements.gap: The broad direct-L1 spectral class has neither the treatment Ls condition nor the outcome-code condition required for the published ACE class.
statements.consumer: A referee can audit the one-way subclass inclusion, exact eligibility, constants, and zero-radius extension.

statements.statement:
The following conclusions are separate facts on separately defined, incomparable classes.  Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs.  Select and fix the one once-for-all witness bank whose existence is asserted in \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) using \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\).  Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), the broad fixed-separated non-Gaussian class has the existence-level fixed-bank rate
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Conditional on that selected bank, the witnessing statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\); no effective construction of the bank is asserted.  Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection defined in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) diagnoses an incompatibility internal to the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.  The positive lower-bound claim from that theorem is not relied upon here.  These facts do not constitute a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy or a local-to-Gaussian frontier, and no equality or inclusion between the two classes is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
The first fact follows from \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\).  That theorem selects and fixes one once-for-all bank supplied by \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) and constants independent of \(n\), and on every stated index proves
\[
 c/n\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le C/n.
\]
It proves the upper bound using the measurable statistic associated with that selected bank and does not construct the bank effectively.  Inspection of \(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\) shows that membership uses \(\bar g_n\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\), but no supplied outcome code or outcome-code radius.  Inspection of \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) likewise shows that, conditional on the selected bank, the statistic uses \(Y\) and \(T-\bar g_n(X)\), but not \(\widehat q_n,\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\).  This proves the fixed-separated non-Gaussian assertion, including fixed nonzero treatment-code error.

For the separate Gaussian class, \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) proves that every member has \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  When that class is nonempty, the same proposition and \(\text{def:minimax-risks}\) give
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]
Its argument uses the simultaneous exact conditional-mean equation, bounded observed outcome, and nondegenerate Gaussian treatment residual: a bounded outcome has a bounded conditional mean, whereas a nonzero coefficient multiplying the Gaussian residual has unbounded support.  Hence the incompatibility is internal to those simultaneous source assumptions, and no positive Gaussian lower bound is used.  Since the two conclusions concern separately defined classes and neither inclusion nor equality has been established, they are separate facts and imply neither a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian minimax dichotomy nor a shrinking-separation frontier.
statements.justification: The legacy graph node records two separate facts: the fixed-separated non-Gaussian existence-level rate and the zero-target bounded-outcome Gaussian source diagnostic.
statements.gap: Earlier framing incorrectly invited a minimax comparison between incomparable classes.
statements.consumer: Use the first fact as a fixed-separation rate theorem and the second only to audit the source assumptions; this node is not a dichotomy or local frontier.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Then \(\kappa_4(\eta)=-2\), \(M(i\pi/2)=0\), and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(a=\pi/2\). Represent the stipulated mixture as \(\eta=R+E\), where \(R\) is symmetric Rademacher, \(E\sim N(0,1)\), and \(R\perp E\). Then
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]=e^{z^2/2}\cosh z,
\qquad
M(ia)=e^{-a^2/2}\cos a=0.
\]
Moreover, \(E_P[\eta]=0\), \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), and independence gives
\[
E_P[\eta^4]
=E_P[R^4]+6E_P[R^2]E_P[E^2]+E_P[E^4]
=1+6+3=10.
\]
The centered fourth-cumulant identity therefore yields
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=E_P[\eta^4]-3E_P[\eta^2]^2=10-3\cdot2^2=-2.
\]

The characteristic function of \(\eta\) is
\[
\phi(t)=E_P[e^{it\eta}]=e^{-t^2/2}\cos t.
\]
For any deterministic \(d\in\mathbb R\), symmetry of \(\eta\) gives
\[
E_P[\cos\{t(\eta+d)\}]=\phi(t)\cos(td).
\]
Differentiation under the expectation is valid because the Gaussian mixture has a finite first moment. Hence
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{t(\eta+d)\}]
=-\frac{d}{dt}\{\phi(t)\cos(td)\}.
\]
Since \(\phi(a)=0\) and \(\phi'(a)=-e^{-a^2/2}\), evaluation at \(a=\pi/2\) gives
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=e^{-a^2/2}\cos(ad).
\]
The variable \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), so \(\eta\perp X\) implies \(\eta\perp D_n\). Conditioning on \(D_n\) and using \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\),
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(aZ_n)]
=e^{-a^2/2}E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P[\cos(\pi D_n/2)].
\]
The direct \(L^1(P_X)\) premise is exactly
\[
E_P|D_n|=\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
Using \(1-\cos u\le |u|\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/\pi\),
\[
E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
\ge1-aE_P|D_n|
\ge1-\frac{\pi}{2}\frac1\pi
=\frac12.
\]
Thus
\[
c_0:=\frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}>0
\]
is a uniform population relevance and division bound. The cutoff in \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}\) prevents division below \(c_0/2\).

For the risk calculation define
\[
W_i:=Z_{n,i}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\qquad
V_i:=\{Y_i-\theta_0(P)Z_{n,i}\}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\]
and let \(\bar W_n=\mathbb P_nW\) and \(\bar V_n=\mathbb P_nV\). The residual identity is
\[
Y-\theta_0(P)Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi,
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)D_n.
\]
For every \(d\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P[\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=\operatorname{Im}\{e^{iad}\phi(a)\}=0.
\]
Consequently, conditioning on \(X\) gives
\[
E_P[b_n(X)\sin(aZ_n)]=0.
\]
Because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), the conditional-mean restriction gives
\[
E_P[\xi\sin(aZ_n)]
=E_P\!\left[E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\sin(aZ_n)\right]=0.
\]
Therefore \(E_P[V_i]=0\).

The clipping definition and the range restriction imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely. Set
\[
b_{\max}:=C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g.
\]
Then \(|b_n(X)|\le b_{\max}\). The conditional sub-Gaussian condition entails \(E_P[\xi^2]\le K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for a finite universal constant \(K_{\xi}\) determined only by the convention for the conditional \(\psi_2\)-norm. Since \(|\sin u|\le1\),
\[
E_P[V_i^2]
\le2b_{\max}^2+2K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2
=:K_V.
\]
Also, \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), and \(|\sin u|\le1\) imply
\[
E_P[W_i^2]
\le E_P[Z_n^2]
\le2E_P[\eta^2]+2E_P[D_n^2]
\le4+8C_g^2
=:K_W.
\]
These bounds verify the integrability needed for conditioning, differentiation, and the variance calculations.

Let \(\mathcal A_n=\{\bar W_n\ge c_0/2\}\), the event on which the sample ratio is used. Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase distance from \(\theta_0(P)\). Thus, on \(\mathcal A_n\),
\[
|\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)|^2
\le\frac{\bar V_n^2}{\bar W_n^2}
\le\frac{4\bar V_n^2}{c_0^2}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n^c\), clipping bounds the squared loss by \(4C_{\theta}^2\). If \(m_W=E_P[W_i]\), then \(m_W\ge c_0\). Independent and identically distributed sampling and Chebyshev's inequality therefore give
\[
P(\mathcal A_n^c)
\le P\!\left(|\bar W_n-m_W|\ge\frac{c_0}{2}\right)
\le\frac{4\operatorname{Var}_P(W_i)}{nc_0^2}
\le\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}.
\]
The same sampling condition and \(E_P[V_i]=0\) yield
\[
E_P[\bar V_n^2]
=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_P(V_i)}{n}
\le\frac{K_V}{n}.
\]
Combining the two events,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
&\le\frac{4K_V}{nc_0^2}
+4C_{\theta}^2\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}\\
&=\frac{4K_V+16C_{\theta}^2K_W}{c_0^2}\,\frac1n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The constant depends only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), and not on \(P\), \(n\), the supplied outcome code, or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). This proves the proposition, including its support, relevance, positivity, integrability, and fallback boundary conditions.

statements.statement:
For \(n\ge2\), there is \(K<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(R_1\), such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) with \(|I_a|\ge1\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|^2\right]
 +E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|^2\right]
 \le \frac{K}{|I_a|}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(m_a=|I_a|\) and let \(\mathbb P_a\) denote the empirical average on that half-sample.  The observations within \(I_a\) are independent under \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\).  Uniformly on \(|z|\le R_1\), the exponential series gives
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)
 =\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^p}{p!}(\mathbb P_a-P)Z_n^p
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)
 =\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^p}{p!}(\mathbb P_a-P)(YZ_n^p).
\]
For every square-integrable random variable \(W\), independence and centering give
\[
 \left\|(\mathbb P_a-P)W\right\|_{L^2(P^{\otimes m_a})}
 =m_a^{-1/2}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_P(W)}
 \le m_a^{-1/2}\lVert W\rVert_{L^2(P)}.
\]

Membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the clipping bound \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), and \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\) imply that, for a class-uniform constant \(C_Z<\infty\),
\[
 \lVert Z_n\rVert_{L^p(P)}\le C_Z\sqrt p,
 \qquad p\ge2.
\]
Also \(Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi\).  The boundedness of \(q_0\) and \(\theta_0\), the treatment sub-Gaussian bound, and the unconditional moment consequence of the conditional sub-Gaussian bound on \(\xi\) give
\[
 \lVert Y\rVert_{L^4(P)}\le C_Y
\]
uniformly over the class.  Consequently, for every integer \(p\ge1\),
\[
 \lVert Z_n^p\rVert_{L^2(P)}
 =\lVert Z_n\rVert_{L^{2p}(P)}^p
 \le(C\sqrt p)^p
\]
and, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \lVert YZ_n^p\rVert_{L^2(P)}
 \le\lVert Y\rVert_{L^4(P)}
     \lVert Z_n\rVert_{L^{4p}(P)}^p
 \le C(C\sqrt p)^p.
\]
The terms at \(p=0\) are bounded by the same conclusion after enlarging \(C\).

Minkowski's inequality now yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|\right\|_2
 &\le m_a^{-1/2}\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}
   \frac{R_1^p(C\sqrt p)^p}{p!},\\
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|\right\|_2
 &\le Cm_a^{-1/2}\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}
   \frac{R_1^p(C\sqrt p)^p}{p!}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the \(p=0\) summand is interpreted as a separate finite constant.  For \(p\ge1\), the bound \(p!\ge(p/e)^p\) shows that the \(p\)-th summand is at most \((CR_1e/\sqrt p)^p\); hence the series is finite.  The same summable \(L^2\) majorant justifies the preceding termwise operations.  Squaring the two inequalities and enlarging the uniform constant proves
\[
 E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|^2\right]
 +E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|^2\right]
 \le\frac K{m_a}.
\]

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the class's \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code restriction and clipping imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely and \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Hence
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|H_n(z)-1|
 \le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), then \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) throughout \(\{|z|\le R_1\}\), and \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros there with multiplicity.
statements.proof_tex:
Membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) gives directly
\[
 E_P|D_n|
 =\lVert g_0-\bar g_n\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
The treatment regression and its clipped supplied code both take values in \([-C_g,C_g]\).  Therefore
\[
 |D_n|=|g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)|\le2C_g
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
For every \(w\in\mathbb C\),
\[
 e^w-1=w\int_0^1e^{tw}\,dt,
 \qquad
 |e^w-1|\le|w|e^{|w|}.
\]
Consequently, uniformly over \(|z|\le R_1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |H_n(z)-1|
 &\le E_P|e^{zD_n}-1|\\
 &\le |z|E_P[|D_n|e^{|z||D_n|}]\\
 &\le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0=\{4R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\}^{-1}\), this upper bound is at most \(1/4\), and hence
\[
 |H_n(z)|\ge1-|H_n(z)-1|\ge\frac34,
 \qquad |z|\le R_1.
\]
Thus \(H_n\) is zero-free throughout the disk.  By \(\text{lem:observable-factorization}\), \(F_n=MH_n\).  Multiplication by a nonvanishing analytic function neither creates a zero nor changes a zero's multiplicity, which proves the final assertion.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  The support restriction in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) gives
\[
 |Y|\le C_q
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{1}
\]
Because \(Y\) is bounded, all conditional expectations below exist.  Conditional Jensen's inequality gives
\[
 |q_0(X)|=|E_P[Y\mid X]|
 \le E_P[|Y|\mid X]\le C_q, \tag{2}
\]
and, on writing \(m(X,T)=E_P[Y\mid X,T]\),
\[
 |m(X,T)|\le E_P[|Y|\mid X,T]\le C_q
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{3}
\]
By the residual definitions,
\[
 Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\eta+\xi,
 \qquad
 \eta=T-g_0(X).
\]
Both \(q_0(X)\) and \(\eta\) are \(\sigma(X,T)\)-measurable.  The restriction \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) therefore implies
\[
 m(X,T)=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\eta
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{4}
\]

Suppose for contradiction that \(\theta_0(P)\ne0\).  Under the Gaussian-treatment restriction,
\[
 \theta_0(P)\eta
 \sim N(0,\theta_0(P)^2\sigma^2).
\]
The boundary condition \(\sigma>0\) makes this Gaussian nondegenerate.  Thus
\[
 A=\{\theta_0(P)\eta>2C_q\}
\]
has strictly positive probability.  On the intersection of \(A\) with the probability-one event on which (2)--(4) hold,
\[
 m(X,T)=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\eta
 \ge-C_q+\theta_0(P)\eta>C_q,
\]
contradicting (3).  Hence \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  Since \(n\) and \(P\) were arbitrary, this holds throughout \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).

Now suppose that the class is nonempty.  The statistic \(\widetilde\theta\equiv0\) is admissible in \(\text{def:minimax-risks}\).  For every class member,
\[
 (\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2=0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)|)=0.
\]
Both minimax criteria are nonnegative.  Taking the class supremum and then the infimum over all statistics proves
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus the zero statistic is minimax for both losses.  No overlap, positivity, rank, division, or inverse condition is used.  The finiteness of \(C_q\) supplies the support bound, \(\sigma>0\) supplies nondegenerate Gaussian support, and nonemptiness is needed only for the minimax display.

statements.statement:
Specialize to \(k=4\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a},
 \qquad
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\},
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and the direct condition \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Then
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
\]
\(t_a\) is the first positive characteristic zero, and \(E[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]=0\) for every real \(d\).  If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge A_a/2.
\]
Define
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is \(C<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that uniformly over these laws,
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n a^{-2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, for \(\Delta_a=2a^4\), the condition is \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\Delta_a^{1/4}/(2^{1/4}\pi)\), and the risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)\right\}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Independence of \(G_{\circ}\) and \(S\) gives
\[
 M_a(z)
 =E[e^{z\sqrt{1-a^2}G_{\circ}}]E[e^{zaS}]
 =\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az).
\]
Since the fourth derivative at zero of \(\log\cosh(az)\) is \(-2a^4\), the cumulant definition gives \(\kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4\).  Its characteristic function is
\[
 \varphi_a(t)=M_a(it)
 =\exp\!\left(-\frac{1-a^2}{2}t^2\right)\cos(at).
\]
The exponential factor is positive, so the first positive zero is \(t_a=\pi/(2a)\), and for every real \(d\),
\[
 E[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]
 =\operatorname{Im}\{e^{it_ad}\varphi_a(t_a)\}=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \varphi_a'(t_a)
 =-a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}=-A_a.
\]
Differentiation under the expectation is justified because \(\eta_a\) has moments of every order.  Differentiating \(e^{itd}\varphi_a(t)\) and taking real parts at \(t_a\) yields
\[
 E[(\eta_a+d)\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]=A_a\cos(t_ad).
\]
Since \(D_n\) is measurable in \(X\) and \(\eta_a\perp X\), conditioning on \(D_n\) gives
\[
 m_a:=E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]=A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)].
\]
The direct \(L^1(P_X)\) premise is exactly \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Hence \(1-\cos u\le|u|\) and \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) imply
\[
 E_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge1-t_aE_P|D_n|
 \ge\frac12,
\]
so \(m_a\ge A_a/2>0\).  This is the required overlap condition.

Put
\[
 W=Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n),\qquad
 V=Y\sin(t_aZ_n),\qquad
 R=(Y-\theta_0Z_n)\sin(t_aZ_n).
\]
The residual identity is \(Y-\theta_0Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi\).  Conditional shift annihilation gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)\sin(t_aZ_n)]=0,
\]
and outcome mean independence gives
\[
 E_P[\xi\sin(t_aZ_n)]
 =E_P[\sin(t_aZ_n)E_P(\xi\mid X,T)]=0.
\]
Therefore \(E_P[R]=0\) and \(E_P[V]=\theta_0m_a\), establishing the population identifying moment separately from the sample ratio.

Clipping and the range condition give \(|D_n|\le2C_g\).  Since \(E[\eta_a^2]=1\) and \(\eta_a\perp D_n\),
\[
 E_P[W^2]\le E_P[Z_n^2]
 =1+E_P[D_n^2]\le1+4C_g^2=:K_W.
\]
Also \(|b_n(X)|\le C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g\).  The conditional sub-Gaussian premise implies \(E_P[\xi^2]\le c_{\psi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for a universal convention-dependent \(c_{\psi}<\infty\).  Thus
\[
 E_P[R^2]
 \le2(C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g)^2+2c_{\psi}\psi_{\xi}^2=:K_R.
\]
Both constants are uniform in \(a,n,P\).

Write \(\overline W=\mathbb P_nW\), \(\overline V=\mathbb P_nV\), and \(\mathcal E=\{\overline W\ge A_a/4\}\).  Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) is a contraction and \(\theta_0\) belongs to that interval.  On \(\mathcal E\),
\[
 |\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0|
 \le\frac{|\mathbb P_nR|}{\overline W}
 \le\frac4{A_a}|\mathbb P_nR|.
\]
Independence and \(E_P[R]=0\) yield
\[
 E_P[(\mathbb P_nR)^2]\le K_R/n.
\]
On \(\mathcal E^c\), the squared error is at most \(C_{\theta}^2\), while Chebyshev's inequality and \(m_a\ge A_a/2\) give
\[
 P(\mathcal E^c)
 \le P(|\overline W-m_a|\ge A_a/4)
 \le\frac{16K_W}{nA_a^2}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2]
 \le\frac{16(K_R+C_{\theta}^2K_W)}{nA_a^2}.
\]
The independent deterministic bound \(|\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0|^2\le4C_{\theta}^2\), together with
\[
 A_a^{-2}=a^{-2}\exp\!\left\{\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right\},
\]
proves the first risk display.  Finally \(\Delta_a=2a^4\) gives
\[
 a=2^{-1/4}\Delta_a^{1/4},
 \qquad
 t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac12
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and
\[
 a^{-2}\exp\!\left\{\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right\}
 =\sqrt2e^{-\pi^2/4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left\{\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right\}.
\]
Absorbing the fixed prefactor into \(C\) completes the proof.  No supplied outcome code is used.

statements.statement:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.
statements.justification: This is the strongest closed local-to-Gaussian result supported by the current proof spine: an exact published ACE specialization and an explicit pathwise spectral upper bound.
statements.gap: It supplies upper benchmarks but no full cumulant-only converse, quantitative contour-modulus theorem, adaptive switching theorem, or coverage result.
statements.consumer: A downstream analysis can use the displayed eligibility test and risk formula to compare finite-order and pathwise spectral procedures without mistaking either for the unresolved minimax frontier.
statements.proof_tex:
For the first conclusion, fix \(n\).  Since \(\delta_n>0\), apply \(\text{lem:jms-ace-theorem-five-four}\) with its positive separation constant replaced by \(\delta_n\).  The resulting law class is exactly \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\), because every other restriction in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) is unchanged.  The quantities \(a_{1,n}\), \(b_{1,n}\), and \(a_2\) are unchanged, whereas the source theorem's \(b_{2,n}\) becomes
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
 (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}^{-1}.
\]
Therefore the displayed local eligibility condition is precisely the eligibility condition of the cited theorem after this substitution.  The hypotheses \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), together with the requirement that all logarithms and denominators be defined, supply its positivity and boundary conditions.  The cited theorem consequently gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|)\\
 &\quad\le C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
 +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{35mm}+64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
 \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
 (\gamma n)^{-1/2}\Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
This is \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  Taking the smaller of this numerical bound and a separately valid DML bound is only an oracle comparison: no sample-measurable selector or minimax lower bound follows from comparing two upper bounds.

For the second conclusion, every displayed path hypothesis is exactly a hypothesis of \(\text{lem:gaussian-rademacher-l1-benchmark}\), including the direct condition
\[
 \lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
That lemma therefore gives, without an appeal to Lyapunov's inequality, the formulas for \(M_a\), \(\kappa_4(\eta_a)\), \(t_a\), and \(A_a\); the exact shift-annihilation identity; the denominator lower bound under \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\); the displayed computable clipped ratio; and its uniform mean-squared-error bound.  Substituting \(\Delta_a=2a^4\) gives
\[
 a=(\Delta_a/2)^{1/4},
 \qquad
 t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac12
 \iff
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and elementary algebra converts the first risk display into
\[
 C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)\right\},
\]
after enlarging the constant \(C\) by the fixed factor arising from \(a^{-2}=\sqrt2\,\Delta_a^{-1/2}\).  This proves the second conclusion under the stated \(L^1(P_X)\) premise.  The first result is only an ACE upper benchmark and the second concerns one explicit Gaussian--Rademacher path; neither supplies a converse or a uniform theorem over the class defined solely by cumulant separation.  Hence the full minimax phase diagram is not determined.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), the same externally supplied deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) is clipped and used in both branches; the pair may vary with \(n\) but is fixed before the independent inference sample is drawn.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment with the definitional residual \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\); the spectral branch imposes independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian noise, while the Gaussian comparator branch is exactly the known-variance bounded-outcome class of Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used; spectral relevance is a positive winding number with a boundary modulus bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The deterministic radii \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) are nonincreasing, so the uncertainty balls are nested. The spectral estimator uses only \(\bar g_n\); the Gaussian comparison uses the same clipped pair and radii.

estimand_functional: There exist a once-for-all deterministic witness bank satisfying \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\) and \(C<\infty\) such that, after that one bank is selected and fixed, the associated \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) is measurable and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]\le C/n\).

The simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded observed-outcome, and nondegenerate Gaussian treatment-noise assumptions stated around Theorem 3.2 force \(\theta_0=0\). The positive lower-bound claim is not relied upon; this is a source-assumption diagnostic, not a Gaussian comparator arm.

Finite-order orthogonal PLM moments and a Gaussian characterization inform the setting, but do not give exact all-shift transform annihilation or the present existence-level fixed-bank uniform minimax theorem.
Location-family completeness results inform transform null spaces, but do not give learned-residual PLM contour ratios or their mean-squared-error theorem.
Observable transform-zero testing informs zero inheritance, but does not give learned-residual PLM contour ratios or their mean-squared-error theorem.

tldr: Complex zeros of the treatment-noise moment generating function yield exact all-shift annihilation, and observable learned-residual transforms identify \(\theta_0\) by a contour ratio. Compactness non-effectively supplies at least one finite uniformly conditioned bank; selecting and fixing one such bank yields an associated measurable split-sample statistic with uniform \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) MSE under sufficiently small fixed direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code error and no outcome learner. This is an existence-level fixed-bank minimax result, not an algorithm for obtaining the bank. Separately, the simultaneous bounded-outcome Gaussian assumptions stated around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2 force \(\theta_0=0\); this is a source-assumption diagnostic, not a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian dichotomy. The shrinking-separation frontier and uniform inference remain open.

project_justification.gap: Finite-order orthogonal and ACE methods provide nuisance-dependent upper guarantees, while classical location-family work recognizes transform zeros; neither supplies the present learned-residual contour estimator with a once-for-all non-effectively selected bank and matched fixed-separation minimax MSE. The simultaneous bounded-outcome Gaussian assumptions around Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2 instead force the target to vanish and therefore serve only as a source-assumption diagnostic.
project_justification.niche: Independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian treatment noise creates an exact null space for every location shift induced by treatment-code error. A sufficiently small fixed direct \(L^1(P_X)\) residual contamination preserves the observable zero geometry, so one selected contour bank permits estimation without a supplied outcome regression.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the exact annihilator and observable contour identities, zero localization, existence of a non-effective finite uniformly conditioned witness bank, empirical-transform control, selected-bank measurability, and matching \(c/n\) and \(C/n\) MSE bounds after one witness is selected and fixed. It retains the exact Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 ACE upper comparison only on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\), and treats the bounded-outcome Gaussian calculation solely as a separate source-assumption diagnostic.

The simultaneous bounded-outcome Gaussian assumptions stated around that paper's Theorem 3.2 instead force \(\theta_0=0\), so its positive lower-bound claim is not used. \cite{Mattner1992} and \cite{HuShiu2022} inform location-family completeness and observable-zero testing, but not learned-residual PLM contour ratios or MSE. \cite{DinhGhoshTranTran2021} informs zero localization. \cite{ChackoViceira2003} supplies complex and spectral GMM precedent, but not treatment-residual nuisance annihilation without an outcome learner. \cite{ReizingerEtAl2025} studies linear ICA treatment-effect estimation, not this residual-contour fixed-error PLM result. \cite{LeeMesters2024} studies weak-non-Gaussian inference in linear simultaneous equations, not this PLM construction or its open phase diagram. These are targeted distinctions, not claims that transform zeros are new, not priority claims, and not an exhaustive review.
technical_internal_limitation: The analytic factorization, contour identity, zero localization, compact-open finite-subcover argument, nuisance zero-free bound, empirical-transform \(L^2\) control, selected-bank measurability, failure-event bound, and Le Cam submodel are proved. The finite subcover is non-effective: no computable radii, conditioning modulus, bank enumeration, or quantitative dependence on shrinking \(\delta_n\) is available. Effective bank construction, the shrinking-separation phase diagram, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and matching local lower bounds remain open.
honest_scope: The matched \(n^{-1}\) MSE result is an existence-level fixed-separation theorem conditional on selecting and fixing one compactness witness bank; it does not give an algorithm for obtaining that bank. It allows sufficiently small fixed nonzero direct \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code error and uses no supplied outcome code. The ACE comparison is only an upper-guarantee comparison on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) under the exact published eligibility condition and constants. The bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection forces \(\theta_0=0\) and is used only to diagnose the simultaneous source assumptions, not as a positive Gaussian lower-bound arm or a Gaussian-versus-non-Gaussian dichotomy. The local-to-Gaussian frontier, effective construction, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and matching local lower bounds remain open.
